pr_title: Normalize before comparing hostname and scheme
pr_body:
Scheme and hostname should be normalised to lowercase before comparing. [`URI#normalize`](https://github.com/ruby/uri/blob/b50d37f7a193991c56bda7f94e8dd6fec0bb3f7f/lib/uri/generic.rb#L1328-L1338) does just that.

Fixes #20944

Note that if we don't enforce lowercase, people may an uppercase I as a lowercase L, like in the latter of the following:

- https://paypal.com
- https://paypaI.com

I don't know if blocking uppercase was the intention behind the original code?

issue_context.title: Verification of links fail when uppercase letters are used in domain name
issue_context.body: ### Steps to reproduce the problem 1. Copying the verification HTML snippet from my Mastodon account preferences to the entry page of my home page: `Mastodon` 2. Adding my homepage to my "Profile metadata" in the Mastodon account preferences: `https://Karl-Voit.at` using upper and lower case characters just like my name is written normally. 3. Verification in the Mastodon profile view fails (does not have green background color). ... ### Expected behaviour Verificaton URL check should be case insensitive and Karl-Voit.at should be recognized as identical to karl-voit.at ### Actual behaviour URL-Verification in the Mastodon profile view fails (does not have green background color) as long as the URL contains upper case letters ### Detailed description The Mastodon URL verification check does seem to assume that at least any domain of an URL consists of lower case letters only. Therefore, `Example.com` and `example.com` are not detected as the same URL. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035 does define domain names as case insensitive (for most use-cases like this one here). The issue may be related to #20807. ### Specifications Mastodon v4.0.2
comments: Hmm, the code appears to downcase everything before comparing, so this is odd.
However I can reproduce, so it's definitely an issue.

Aha, I think it's this line here. https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/main/app/models/account/field.rb#L49

We need to lowercase for this comparison to pass, otherwise it doesn't even attempt validation.

The comment in that method seems to indicate that line is there to make sure it's not an international domain name. I don't think using uppercase qualifies as an IDN, but nevertheless I'd want to know why IDNs are not verifiable before making the fix

@toby-1-kenobi IDN verification was disabled recently to avoid the potential for phishing (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDN_homograph_attack)

Arguably upper case letters have a slight potential for that (for example Il), I'm unsure if to the extent that we shouldn't verify them.

Came across this as I'm fixing another verification issue; `normalized_host` in addressable will return punycode (`xn--...`) for IDN names.

So there's no Unicode concern there (as one side is guaranteed to be ASCII) and it is safe to do `parsed_url.normalized_host == parsed_url.host.downcase`.

Just came across this bug as well and took some time to find this Issue. It's not obvious. Additionally, this causes an accessibility problem -- screen readers find it hard to read thingsthatarealllowercase (things that are all lower case). I've been making it a point to useCamelCaseInMyUrls.

review_comments: The added coverage here (http vs https urls) seems useful on its own, but not related to the actual change here (non-ascii chars in url values)...?
